rules.citation: San Diego Mun. Code §98.0701 et seq.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies in residential rental property subject to Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 7, terminated for at-fault or no-fault just cause.
rules.disclaimer: Not legal advice. Based only on the cited sources and the listed address facts.
rules.interaction: Relocation assistance under this Division is credited against any other relocation assistance required by federal, state or other local law.
rules.key_value: 2 months' actual rent (3 months for senior or disabled tenant)
rules.quoted_span:
(i) Unless section 98.0706(c)(1)(A)(ii) applies, the direct 
payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to 
two months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in 
effect at the date of the notice.  
 
(ii) If the tenant is a senior or disabled, the direct payment 
to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to three 
months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect

rules.coverage_conditions: Any dwelling or unit intended for human habitation, including units in a mobile home park; applies to landlords and to persons who sell, license or provide algorithmic devices.
rules.disclaimer: Not legal advice. Based only on the cited sources and the listed address facts.
rules.exemptions: Software that publishes reports from aggregated nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old or from public information, without recommending future rates; software used to set rates or income limits under affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.quoted_span:
It is unlawful for a Landlord to use an Algorithmic Device to set rental rates or
                  occupancy levels for Residential Real Property. For each month a violation of
                  Section 8- 3702( b) exists or continues, and for each Residential Rental Property
                  a Landlord uses an Algorithmic Device, it shall constitute a separate and distinct
                  violation.
rules.requirement: No person may sell, license or provide an algorithmic device to a landlord, and no landlord may use one to set rental rates or occupancy levels; each month and each property is a separate violation.
rules.title: Santa Ana algorithmic rent-setting ban (Ordinance No. NS-3090)

rules.disclaimer: Not legal advice. Based only on the cited sources and the listed address facts.
rules.exemptions: Dwellings with four or fewer housing spaces; licensed hotels and motels; commercial and industrial space; new redevelopment dwellings of 25 or more units; low-rent public housing; buildings converted to dwelling use on or after October 1, 1983; first rental of a new dwelling.
rules.key_value: 4% or CPI increase, whichever is less
rules.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of a lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord of any dwelling as defined in § 260-1 may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than four percent or the percentage difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less.
rules.requirement: A landlord may not increase rent by more than 4% or the CPI change over the lease term, whichever is less, only once in any 12-month period. Vacant-unit rent may exceed that only for registered capital improvements at set rates.

rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords of rental housing subject to this rent control chapter; this section states no further limits.
rules.disclaimer: Not legal advice. Based only on the cited sources and the listed address facts.
rules.exemptions: Rent increases authorized by this chapter.
rules.quoted_span: No landlord shall after the effective date of this chapter charge any rents in excess of what he or she was receiving from the effective date of this chapter except for increases as authorized by this chapter; nor shall such landlord charge any rents in excess of what he or she was receiving on January 11, 1973, if such excess is in excess of the rental which is authorized by this chapter.
rules.requirement: After the chapter's effective date, a landlord may not charge rent above the rent it was receiving on that date, or above the rent received on January 11, 1973 where the chapter authorizes less, except for increases the chapter authorizes.
rules.title: Jersey City rent control rent ceiling

rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of dwellings covered by the Jersey City Rent Control chapter who have owned the building at least nine months.
rules.disclaimer: Not legal advice. Based only on the cited sources and the listed address facts.
rules.quoted_span: In the event that a landlord cannot meet his or her mortgage payments or operating expenses or does not make a fair return on his or her investment, he or she may apply to the Rent Leveling Board for increased rentals, provided that he or she has owned the building for at least nine months prior to the time he or she applies for an increase.
rules.requirement: A landlord who cannot meet mortgage or operating expenses or does not make a fair return may apply to the Rent Leveling Board for a hardship increase after owning the building at least nine months; no increase may be imposed without Board approval.
rules.title: Jersey City hardship rental increase

rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords seeking cost-of-living increases on dwellings covered by the Jersey City Rent Control chapter.
rules.disclaimer: Not legal advice. Based only on the cited sources and the listed address facts.
rules.quoted_span: Any landlord seeking a cost-of-living rental increase shall notify the tenant in writing at least 30 days prior to the effective date of the increase as required by law of the calculations involved in computing the increase
rules.requirement: A landlord seeking a cost-of-living rent increase must give the tenant written notice at least 30 days before it takes effect, stating the CPI and other calculations, the allowable percentage under §260-3, and the tenant's right to contest within six months.
rules.title: Jersey City cost-of-living rent increase notice procedure

rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords seeking service or capital improvement surcharges on dwellings covered by the Jersey City Rent Control chapter.
rules.disclaimer: Not legal advice. Based only on the cited sources and the listed address facts.
rules.exemptions: Emergency major capital improvements need no prior Board approval; only one major capital improvement increase per 12-month period, except emergency improvements.
rules.key_value: 15% of legal rent for the first year; depreciation max 10 years (major) / 5 years (minor)
rules.quoted_span: A capital improvement increase resulting hereunder shall not exceed 15% of the legal rent for the first year of such increase.
rules.requirement: A landlord must get Rent Leveling Board approval before imposing a capital improvement or service surcharge, and a capital improvement increase may not exceed 15% of the legal rent in the first year.
rules.title: Jersey City capital improvement and service charge surcharge
